terms.comment: For a habit, Latin often prefers soleō: ut soleō, as I always do (Cic. Att. 2.8.1).

evidence: Quint. 1.1.20: numquam nōn fēcisse sē gaudeat

phrases.latin: crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper: dīc mihi, crās istud, Postume, quandō venit?
phrases.english: ‘Tomorrow I’ll start living,’ you always say, Postumus, ‘tomorrow’: tell me, Postumus, when does this tomorrow come?

phrases.latin: Cicerō meus quid aget? iste vērō sit in sinū semper et complexū meō
phrases.english: and what will my little Cicero do? Let him always be in my lap and in my arms

sources: Lewis & Short: semper · Lewis & Short: soleo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 86, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
